coachQuestion: How do we attack the Braves' lineup tomorrow?
executiveSummary: The 2026-05-26 Red Sox-Braves game is pre-game for Fenway, so this seeded brief uses the completed Red Sox-Braves matchup from 2026-05-17. In that sample, Atlanta hitters saw 146 tracked pitches, put 27 balls in play, produced 12 balls at 95+ mph, and chased 33% of pitches outside the strike zone when they swung. The safest recommendation is narrow: change eye levels, avoid middle cutters to Austin Riley, and protect left-center hard contact.

attackingPlan.title: Do not give Riley a center-cut cutter after contact is timed
attackingPlan.claim: Austin Riley produced a 104.0 mph, 431 ft home run on a 1-2 cutter in zone 5, then later doubled at 101.0 mph on a low changeup. In this sample, he covered both the middle cutter and the low finish pitch.

evidence.description: Austin Riley homered to left center on an 87.7 mph cutter in zone 5; exit velocity 104.0 mph, launch angle 31 degrees, distance 431 ft.
Austin Riley doubled to left on an 88.2 mph changeup below the zone; exit velocity 101.0 mph, launch angle 12 degrees.

attackingPlan.skepticNote: This is one game, not a season-wide Riley weakness map. Keep the claim to pitch selection in the sampled matchup.
attackingPlan.whyItMatters: Riley changed the game on a pitch that looked like a chase or weak-contact setup but caught too much hittable space.
attackingPlan.recommendedAction: Open Riley with either elevated velocity above his barrel path or breaking movement away from zone 5. Do not repeat cutter-to-cutter sequencing once he has fouled off the sinker.

defensiveAlignment.title: Protect left and center field before over-shifting the infield
defensiveAlignment.claim: Atlanta put 27 tracked balls in play in the 2026-05-17 sample. Locations 7 and 8 accounted for 13 of them, and 12 batted balls were hit 95+ mph.

evidence.description: Jorge Mateo doubled on a sharp line drive to left field; exit velocity 103.7 mph, launch angle 13 degrees.
Drake Baldwin hit a 105.6 mph sacrifice fly to center field on a sinker.

defensiveAlignment.skepticNote: The fielding-location distribution is from one completed Braves home game. Treat it as demo evidence, not a permanent spray profile.
defensiveAlignment.whyItMatters: The demo needs a visible defensive recommendation that is evidence-gated and narrow enough to defend.
defensiveAlignment.recommendedAction: Start LF and CF one step deeper and shade the left-center gap against the hard-contact bats; keep the second baseman honest because five tracked balls were fielded in location 4.

pitchingPlan.title: Change Olson's eye level before the finish pitch
pitchingPlan.claim: Ryan Watson struck out Matt Olson after two fastballs up or near the top band and finished with an 89.7 mph cutter for a swinging strike.

evidence.description: Matt Olson fouled a 94.0 mph four-seam fastball above the zone at plate_z 3.834.
Matt Olson struck out swinging on an 89.7 mph cutter in zone 5.

pitchingPlan.skepticNote: Do not generalize this into Olson always chasing. The supported claim is the successful eye-level sequence in this at-bat.
pitchingPlan.whyItMatters: It gives the coach a repeatable sequence with exact pitch evidence instead of a vague 'mix speeds' note.
pitchingPlan.recommendedAction: Use four-seamers to move Olson's sight line up, then finish with a cutter only after the top-band pitch has been shown.

coachActions: Target game: Braves at Red Sox, Fenway Park, 2026-05-26, gamePk 824758.
Evidence seed: Red Sox at Braves, 2026-05-17, gamePk 824923, final Atlanta Braves 8, Boston Red Sox 1.
Against Austin Riley, avoid zone-5 cutters after he has seen sinker velocity in the at-bat.
Against Matt Olson, change eye level with four-seamers before using the cutter as a finish pitch.
Start the outfield with left-center protection; do not oversell this as a season-long spray tendency.
